description: Search and mine the whole database: keywords (the last word also matches as a prefix, for type-ahead), filters on any nutrient, sorting by up to three keys, per 100 g, per 100 kcal or per serving. E.g. foods with at least 20 g protein per 100 kcal and under 5 g sugars sorted by fibre; branded yogurts by protein; supplements by magnesium. Runs in memory: milliseconds. Rows whose values contradict each other (macros over 100 g, energy far from the macros) are left out unless include_inconsistent. Anything missing or only weakly matched comes back with contribute: tell your user it can be added, and add it with add_proof (new_entity, the maker's page or label photos); it is served at once, verified later by another agent.

categories.description: Only rows whose source category contains one of these words, e.g. ["yogurt", "yoghurt"]: excludes yogurt-coated bars and yogurt cheese. With facets, the category facet lists the exact names. Rows a source gives no category are excluded.

datasets.description: Source datasets, e.g. "Foundation", "SR Legacy", "CIQUAL 2025", "Branded", "NIH DSLD", "Health Canada LNHPD". Facets list them.

facets.description: Also count matches by kind, brand, dataset, market and proof rank. Each facet counts what passes every other filter.

fields.description: Values to return per row. Defaults to energy, macros and anything filtered or sorted on. A group name ("vitamin_a") returns each of its keys separately; where and sort take one key.

has.description: Only rows with a known value for each of these properties (registry keys or line:<name>).

market.description: Country code, e.g. US, CA, FR.

max_rank.description: Only rows whose strongest proof is at least this strong (1 strongest).

per.description: per_100g compares foods and products; per_serving covers supplements and products with a serving weight; per_100kcal needs at least 20 kcal on the basis of the row (per 100 g, or per serving), below that the row is left out; native shows each row on its own basis, for mixed lists. Each row says what its values are per in values_per.

q.description: Keywords in any language. Omit to scan everything that matches the filters.

where.description: Ranges on the chosen basis (per). A property is a registry key or a free label line, line:<name> (see label_lines).

unit.description: Free label lines only: the unit of min and max (g, mg, mcg, IU, CFU, billion CFU, ml). Mass converts. Needed when label_lines lists more than one unit for the line; else its one unit (mass lines are stored in mg).

name: query
